tasks.short: Research history and publish scholarly findings

steps.what: Locate, obtain and read actual primary and secondary historical sources for the specific research question
inputs: actual historical research question
actual archive/catalogue records and source texts
outputs: teacher-read historical source collection and provenance limits

steps.what: Conduct historical research through source criticism, contextual interpretation and development of supported findings
inputs: teacher-read historical source collection and provenance limits
actual historiographical question and competing interpretations
outputs: teacher's supported historical findings and evidence limitations

steps.what: Write and check the actual scholarly manuscript, quotations, citations, interpretations and publication permissions
inputs: teacher's supported historical findings and evidence limitations
teacher-read historical source collection and provenance limits
actual publication requirements and permissions
outputs: complete checked authorised historical manuscript and recipient

steps.what: Submit the completed checked authorised historical manuscript to its intended professional journal or publisher
inputs: complete checked authorised historical manuscript and recipient

tasks.design: Configure native catalogue searches and citation fields in {OTHER}, the archive/reference manager, and {DOCS}. The teacher reads and interprets actual sources and writes/checks the scholarly manuscript before the separate {PARTNER_PORTAL} submission; source criticism and historical claims are not generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue navigation and citation formatting can interrupt historical scholarship.
tasks.enabler_now: Native searches and reference fields can reuse actual source identity.
tasks.still_hard: Source provenance, silence and conflicting testimony require historical interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an archival statement from a defensible historical claim.

ambition.what: No automatic historical finding or publication-success claim.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for archive permissions and unpublished research access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native archive searches and citation fields can reduce handling while historical research and interpretation remain expert work.

assumptions: Shares describe unmeasured research with a real manuscript submission, not the prompt time prior.
Archives/publishers provide actual source text and catalogue metadata; the teacher obtains/checks provenance in s1. Missing metadata, permissions or sources require real manual work.
Only discovery navigation and citation formatting change. All reading, historical interpretation, prose and quotation checking remain counted; existing equivalent configuration removes the gain.
Gross provisional saving 4.2 minus 1 hour of reference/search upkeep gives 3.2 net. Submission is negligible and fully retained.
The final manuscript and actual permissions are checked in s3; edits void its submission gate. Book/electronic publication routes require their actual production work and separate measurement.
unknowns: Actual archive discovery and citation handling
research_questions: Do native catalogue/reference settings remove repeated handling in real historical research?

already_counted.description: Read actual sources and complete/check manuscript

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue searches and citation mappings

approvals.approved_version: complete checked authorised historical manuscript and recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 3.2%; actual historical scholarship remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade history examinations

steps.what: Compile and check the actual history examination, source extracts, rubric, student instructions and intended roster/release time
inputs: actual history learning objectives and permitted item bank
actual source extracts, exam constraints and marking criteria
actual examination roster and authorised release time
outputs: complete checked history examination and rubric
checked examination roster and authorised release time

steps.what: Release the completed checked examination to the intended students at the authorised examination time
inputs: complete checked history examination and rubric
actual examination roster and authorised release time

steps.what: Administer the actual examination, explain permitted procedure and handle student/access issues
inputs: released history examination
actual students and examination conditions

steps.what: Grade actual historical arguments and source use against the rubric and complete checked examination feedback/marks
inputs: actual completed student examination submissions
complete checked history examination and rubric
outputs: complete checked student examination feedback and marks

steps.what: Release the completed checked examination feedback and marks to the correct students
inputs: complete checked student examination feedback and marks

tasks.design: Configure native item-bank, source-extract and exam-format reuse in {LMS} and {DOCS}. The teacher checks the actual examination before release, administers it and grades historical reasoning before the separate result release; no automatic essay grading is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated assembly/formatting of actual examination material can consume preparation effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item-bank and exam settings can reuse existing checked structure.
tasks.still_hard: Valid historical assessment depends on question quality and evaluation of contextual arguments.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a defensible interpretation that differs from a model answer.

ambition.what: No automatic marking decision or larger examination capacity claimed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-6 for examination access, assessment policy and staff consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native examination assembly can reduce formatting while administration and history-essay grading remain teacher responsibilities.

assumptions: Shares describe provisional teacher effort for a history essay/source examination, not a measured baseline or closed-question marking claim.
The teacher supplies actual questions, sources and rubric in s1; students produce submissions during s3. New question authoring and all grading remain counted.
Only repeated assembly/formatting changes. Current equivalent item-bank settings remove the gain; no free structured essay interpretation is assumed.
Gross provisional saving 3 minus 1 hour of item-bank/exam-setting upkeep gives 2 net. Both negligible release actions are fully retained.
s1 checks final exam content and actual roster/time for a1; s4 checks final feedback/marks for a2. Any version or recipient change voids its gate; overlapping assignment grading is not added again.
unknowns: Current examination reuse and actual assessment format
research_questions: Which exam assembly steps repeat after existing native item-bank tools?

already_counted.description: Compile/check actual exam and grade student responses

incremental.description: Maintain checked item-bank and exam-format settings

approvals.approved_version: complete checked history examination and rubric; actual examination roster and authorised release time
complete checked student examination feedback and marks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 2%; actual exam administration and grading remain.

tasks.short: Evaluate and grade history classwork, assignments and papers

steps.what: Read actual student historical work and inspect its argument, source use and evidence against the assignment criteria
inputs: actual student classwork/assignment/paper
actual task criteria and relevant historical sources
outputs: teacher's reading of actual student reasoning and evidence

steps.what: Evaluate actual historical reasoning and determine a justified grade and student-specific feedback
inputs: teacher's reading of actual student reasoning and evidence
actual assessment rubric
outputs: teacher's grade decision and specific feedback points

steps.what: Enter, individualize and check the actual grade and feedback for the correct student's work
inputs: teacher's grade decision and specific feedback points
actual student/submission identity
outputs: complete checked student assignment grade and feedback

steps.what: Release the completed checked assignment grade and feedback to the intended student
inputs: complete checked student assignment grade and feedback

tasks.design: Configure native teacher-selected comment snippets and rubric entry in {LMS}. The teacher reads and judges the actual historical work, individualizes/checks feedback and grade, then separately releases the final version; no model assigns a grade or infers misconduct.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated wording/format entry can consume time after the teacher has made actual feedback decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native comment snippets can reuse teacher-chosen wording without generating assessment meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Historical reasoning and source criticism require assessment of the actual submission.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the specific weakness in a student's historical argument.

ambition.what: No automatic grading or educational outcome claim.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for assessment access and approved comment-bank consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native teacher-selected comment snippets can reduce repeated feedback entry while assessment decisions remain human.

assumptions: Shares are provisional teacher marking effort, not a measured grading baseline.

Students supply actual submissions; the teacher supplies rubric and individual feedback decisions in s1/s2. Snippets are manually selected and individualized in s3, not matched by an unproduced feedback code.
Only repeated wording/format entry changes. All reading, grade decisions and final meaning checks remain retained; equivalent current snippets remove the gain.
Gross provisional saving 1.9 minus 0.5 hour of comment-bank upkeep gives 1.4 net. Release is negligible and fully retained.
Final content/student identity is checked in s3 and any change voids the gate. Do not add overlapping exam or records work again.
research_questions: Do teacher-selected snippets save entry effort after student-specific editing and checks?

already_counted.description: Individualize and check actual grade/feedback entry

approvals.approved_version: complete checked student assignment grade and feedback

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 1.4%; all actual historical assessment remains.

tasks.short: Maintain actual attendance, grades and required student records

steps.what: Collect actual attendance observations, authorised grades and required student-record changes for the correct course roster
inputs: actual teacher-observed attendance
actual authorised assessment results and current roster
outputs: teacher-collected student record changes and source identities

steps.what: Resolve actual student, course, assessment and attendance discrepancies before record updates
inputs: teacher-collected student record changes and source identities
actual record requirements and discrepancy evidence

steps.what: Enter/import and check the actual attendance, grade and required student-record updates in the student records application
inputs: teacher-checked actual student-record update sources
existing student/course/assessment identifiers

steps.what: Commit the completed checked actual student-record updates in the existing records application
inputs: complete checked actual student-record updates

tasks.design: Configure native roster views and fixed-column result import from {LMS} into {OTHER}, the student records application, where the teacher actually repeats authorised entries. The teacher captures actual attendance, resolves discrepancies and checks every proposed update before the separate commit; attendance and grades are never inferred.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual authorised grades can require repeated entry across learning and student-record systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import can reuse existing student/course/assessment identity and result fields.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong identity, stale authorisation or exceptional attendance needs manual resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise that a technically valid import would attach a result to the wrong student or assessment.

ambition.what: No automatic attendance inference or grade decision.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-7 for student data, approved imports and employee consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native result import can reduce repeated student-record entry while actual attendance capture and update validation remain human work.

assumptions: Shares describe an unmeasured teacher-owned record-maintenance scenario with actual repeated entry, not grading time or an invented second system.

The teacher produces real attendance observations; authorised assessors produce actual grades; the institution maintains the roster. Collection, missing identifiers and exceptions are counted in s1/s2/s3.
Import requires student ID, course, assessment, result, authorisation and version; missing or unmatched fields stop for manual entry. Non-exported records and attendance capture remain manual.
Native configuration first; existing equivalent sync/import removes the gain. Gross provisional saving 11.3 minus 2 hours of mapping/exception upkeep gives 9.3 net.
The same-system commit is negligible and fully retained. Final identity/content checks occur in s3; no student notification is promised. Do not count grade authoring again.
unknowns: Actual teacher-owned duplicate entry and native import availability
research_questions: Does actual record import save teacher effort after attendance capture, identity checks and exceptions?

incremental.description: Maintain record mappings and handle new import exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 9.3%; actual attendance capture, identity checks and non-exported updates remain.
